done_when: forge sync installs Forge's git hooks in the folder git actually uses (core.hooksPath when set) and still runs the hooks already there, forge doctor reports a hooks folder without them, and a test proves both with a Husky-style hooks path

findings.body: Real Husky hooks do not contain either searched expression. [Husky v9.1.7's installer](https://github.com/typicode/husky/blob/v9.1.7/index.js#L18-L19) generates wrappers that source `.husky/_/h`; the basename-based dispatch lives in that separate file. Consequently, `husky` is false for actual Husky wrappers. After `install_shims` renames them (`src/forge/sync.py:332–336`), Forge executes them with the `.pre-forge` basename. [Husky's dispatcher](https://github.com/typicode/husky/blob/v9.1.7/husky#L3-L6) then looks for `.husky/pre-commit.pre-forge` or `.husky/pre-push.pre-forge` and silently exits when absent, skipping existing checks. The new test at `tests/test_fix_in_a_repo_whose_git_hooks_folder_is_set.py:29–31` inlines the dispatcher into each wrapper, concealing this failure. Handle the actual wrapper/shared-dispatcher layout and exercise that layout through the CLI test to satisfy the hook-preservation requirement.
findings.title: Not done: preserve existing Husky hooks and prove preservation through the CLI

why: In a repo whose git hooks folder is set elsewhere, such as Husky's .husky/_ in myclaw, forge sync installs its git hooks where git never runs them, so Forge's commit and push guards are off
